title: Randomized splitter with rollback replay advisor and smoke-seed lanes
author: Nina Kaur
description:
Motivation: We need a safe, low-friction way to introduce randomized traffic splits for A/B style experiments and fast canaries while preserving reproducibility for automated rollback. This PR implements a randomized-split traffic promoter that: 1) allows exponentially distributed randomized assignments within configured cohorts, 2) attaches a lightweight deterministic seed per request for later replay, and 3) integrates with an offline rollback-replay advisor that can reconstruct failing slices of traffic and suggest targeted rollbacks or micro-bisects.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a new traffic-split plugin that supports 'seeded-random' assignment (configurable per-route), a smoke-seed lane generator that synthesizes a small, representative request stream for early smoke tests, and a rollback-replay advisor with basic heuristics for recommending rollback scopes based on replayed telemetry. The replay advisor can generate a trimmed request batch (using the attached seeds) for the model evaluation harness to reproduce a failure locally.

Design notes: - Randomized assignment is implemented as a deterministic function: hash(route, user_id, seed_epoch) mod 10000 < weight. seed_epoch is part of rollout metadata and can be rotated to create new assignment epochs without changing user identity. This preserves session affinity while making cohort reseeding explicit. - Each assigned request gets an optional 'rw-seed' header that is persisted in request logs and appears in trace spans; the advisor uses these seeds to reconstruct exact request order and payloads for replay. - Smoke-seed lanes: small synthetic stream generators (k=50 by default) derived from production sample distributions to exercise hot-paths before traffic fraction ramps. - Rollback-replay advisor: implements a three-stage flow: identify high delta cohorts -> select top request seeds by error/latency divergence -> produce a replay bundle for local evaluation. Includes safety heuristics to avoid spurious rollback suggestions (minimum confidence threshold, min sample size).

Compatibility and safety: Works with existing session-affinity and shadow lanes. When used with layered canaries the promoter honors 'holdpoints' declared by the rollout controller (it will not increase randomized fraction past holdpoint without operator override). The implementation intentionally avoids global state churn: seed epochs are lightweight numbers patched into rollout specs and are stored in rollout metadata rather than per-request DB records.

Checklist: - [x] Seeded deterministic randomized assignment engine - [x] Request-level seed header propagation and tracing - [x] Smoke-seed lane generator and example config - [x] Rollback-replay advisor prototype (heuristics + replay bundle generation) - [x] Unit tests for assignment and seed propagation - [x] Integration tests for smoke lanes and advisor end-to-end - [x] Console integration for viewing top seeds and replay bundles

Related work: builds on the rollout metadata model introduced in ENG-1873 and complements the replayable-shadow work from PR 612458. Linked Linear tasks ENG-2067 (experiment SDK) and PM-1128 (product rollout UX). Support ticket SUP-3241 required a faster workflow for reproducing cohort regressions which this PR targets.

Notes on scope: This is a medium-sized feature; we ship a conservative advisor first (recommendations only) and will follow up with a curator flow that can auto-schedule micro-rollbacks subject to on-call approval.

Merge rationale: Shipping this gives platform and SRE teams a reproducible primitive for randomized experiments and a low-friction replay path to validate proposed rollbacks. The advisor is opt-in and behind a feature flag by default for pilot tenants.

changed_file_snippets: seeded_splitter.go: assignment = hash32(route + userID + seedEpoch) % 10000 < int(weight*100) // deterministic seeded assignment
replay_advisor.go: // pick top N seeds by delta, serialize minimal replay bundle (seeds + deduped payload references)
review_conversation: Evan Li: Looks solid overall. Two concerns: a) are seeds privacy-safe when persisted? b) can smoke-seeds accidentally become correlated with real PII?
Nina Kaur: Addressed both — seeds are derived from truncated hash of request fingerprint (no raw payload storage), and smoke-seed generator samples anonymized fields only. Added notes and tests.
Sofie Müller: Can the advisor incorrectly recommend rollback for transient infra spikes? Suggest adding a rolling baseline check.
Nina Kaur: Added a rolling baseline comparator and min-sample-size guard; include it in the heuristics.
Arjun Rao: Verified tests and ran integration locally; approving pending CI green.
CI Bot: All checks passed after rerun (lint -> unit -> integration -> e2e smoke).
ci_checks_summary: lint: pass (auto-fix applied), unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e-smoke: pass after one rerun (timing flake on CI runner), security-scan: pass (no secrets), perf-bench: minimal regression (<0.5% p50)
release_notes: Introduce seeded randomized traffic splitter and rollback-replay advisor (opt-in). Adds smoke-seed lane support and console view for replay bundles. No breaking changes to existing rollout specs.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind feature flag 'randomized_splitter_v1'. Recommend enabling for internal pilot first. Retain logs with rw-seed header for at least 72 hours to allow replay bundles to be formed. Advisor recommendations are read-only; automated rollbacks are disabled by default.
manual_tests_run: Ran integration scenario: 1) create randomized rollout at 5% with smoke-seed lane enabled; 2) injected latency spike in cohort; 3) advisor suggested top-15 seeds; 4) used replay bundle to reproduce regression locally; 5) rollback suggestion created and verified by SRE
